title: relationGraph: tickets with relations, placed in columns (API, CLI, HTTP)
description: Add a read-only function relationGraph(project, options) in a new file src/relation-graph.js. Model it on src/roadmap-deps.js, which does a similar job for blockers. The exact result shape is the contract relationGraph (plantool contract show relationGraph) with the types GraphNode and GraphEdge (plantool type list). How to compute it: 1) Load all tickets (project.tickets.list with limit Infinity) and all relations (project.relations.list()). Use every relation type, not only blocks. 2) With options.root (key or id, resolve with project.resolveTicket): keep only relations where at least one end is the root or one of its descendants. Without root keep all. 3) nodes are the tickets that appear in at least one kept relation. hidden is the number of tickets in scope (all tickets, or the root and its descendants) that are not nodes. 4) layer: look only at relations of type blocks, where the source blocks the target. A node without a blocker among the nodes has layer 0. Every other node has layer 1 + the highest layer of its blockers. Blocking relations cannot form a cycle (plantool refuses them), but compute it with a loop or a queue, not with recursion. 5) row: inside each layer sort the nodes by ticket number, then id; row is the position, starting at 0. 6) Sort nodes by layer, then row. If there are more than options.limit (default 200, allowed 1 to 200), keep the first limit nodes and set truncated to true. totalNodes is the number before cutting. 7) edges are the kept relations whose two ends are both in the final nodes, as {sourceId, targetId, type}, sorted by sourceId, targetId, type. layers is the highest layer + 1, or 0 without nodes. Then wire it up the same way dependencies is wired: in src/index.js import it, add p.relationGraph = options => relationGraph(p, options) and export it; in src/index.d.ts add the types; in src/server.js add GET /api/roadmap/graph with the query parameters root and limit next to /api/roadmap/deps; in bin/plantool.js add plantool graph [--root ID] [--limit N] [--format json], which prints one line per edge (KEY title, the type, KEY title) and a last line with the numbers of nodes, edges and hidden tickets, and add it to the usage text. Outside the happy path: an unknown root gives the not-found error of resolveTicket; a limit outside 1 to 200 is a ValidationError; a project without relations returns empty lists and hidden = number of tickets. Known and accepted: rows of blocker and blocked ticket do not line up, so lines may cross. Do not try to solve that here.
why: The picture needs data: which tickets to draw, where, and which lines. Computing it in one place keeps the web view, the CLI and the API identical.

acceptance.text: The result matches the contract relationGraph
plantool graph --format json, project.relationGraph() and GET /api/roadmap/graph return the same data

outcome.summary: Added relationGraph(project, {root, limit}) in src/relation-graph.js: all relation types, layers by blocks chains (Kahn queue), rows by ticket number, limit with truncated, hidden count. Wired into src/index.js (p.relationGraph), src/index.d.ts (GraphNode, GraphEdge, RelationGraphResult), GET /api/roadmap/graph in src/server.js and plantool graph [--root ID] [--limit N] [--format json] in bin/plantool.js. Layers are computed before the limit cut; the reported layers count uses the nodes that are returned.
